evidence.claim: Chesterfield’s tithing buildings explain how a farm community supported its church when cash was scarce.
evidence.quote: Few members could pay cash around 1900, so grains, vegetables, eggs and farm animals were instead paid "in kind".

evidence.claim: Franklin’s founders thought they were settling in Utah Territory in 1860, but the town was in Washington Territory.
evidence.quote: The town was founded by Mormon pioneers led by Thomas S. Smart on April 14, 1860, in what was then Washington Territory, although at the time it was believed the settlement was within the bounds of Utah Territory.

evidence.claim: The townsite itself was platted into square blocks in 1864, before the territorial uncertainty had been resolved.
evidence.quote: The area within the town limits was platted into square blocks in 1864.

evidence.claim: An 1872 survey settled its position in Idaho Territory, about a mile north of Utah’s boundary.
evidence.quote: Its political status remained ambiguous until an 1872 survey determined the townsite was in Idaho Territory about 1-mile (1.6 km) north of the Utah Territory border.

flags: No highway construction or designation history is cached. The history paragraph therefore explains the emigrant corridor and changing transport connections, without equating the modern road with the Oregon Trail.

Visit Idaho gives 114 miles and 2 hours 13 minutes; archived FHWA gives 127 miles and 2.5 hours. Copy attributes the Visit Idaho figures. Detailed curves, grades and driving character are sparsely documented.
Dropped the blanket claim that the towns were settled by Latter-day Saint pioneers: Grace’s cache explicitly says it was not originally settled by Mormon pioneers.

Dropped Chesterfield’s complete abandonment by the 1930s and implication of an uninterrupted surviving amusement hall. The detailed cache records later residents, a 1958 store closure and a ruined hall restored in 1999–2003.
Only secondary sources support current geyser timing and Chesterfield tours; omitted schedules and access promises. The practical checked date is a cache review date.

Travel follows increasing strip miles from Wyoming toward Utah. Chesterfield is a separate excursion placed between Soda Springs and Grace, via the Bancroft area; no unsupported turn-by-turn detour is supplied.
Bear River Massacre is documented only by brief date/location mentions here, without participants or a community account. Omitted rather than turning it into a passing scenic-history reference.
